gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 identifies the later multiplication routine using cycle-entry diagonals instead of circulant eigenvalues. It does not identify the distinct extraction defect in which the old rule fixes a cycle and mixes Fourier modes, omits the unitary normalization, and fails to transpose the Fourier row into the component column.

ISSUE-001 supports only the left-side diagnosis that cycle-entry diagonals are not the Fourier multipliers of the selected circulant components. Gold I002 also contains the independent right-side obligation: computing the right selected sum requires applying the component routine to B_k^*ΔA^* with conjugation and inverse shifts. That distinct failure is not recognized by ISSUE-001, so its partial left-side coverage is insufficient.

ISSUE-002 diagnoses selecting frequencies along the wrong axis and an unrelated 1/n output scaling. It does not recognize that the rectangular caller passes m-by-n and n-by-p inputs to a square n-by-n top-k helper, causing out-of-contract dimension failures and requiring dimension inference from each transformed input.

ISSUE-003 concerns an invalid finite-n expectation/norm calculation for uniform-entry random matrices. Gold I006 instead concerns applying a concentration theorem whose stated group hypotheses exclude disconnected O(n), requiring a separate SO(n)∪SO(n)J decomposition and averaging argument. The prediction provides no diagnosis of that group-hypothesis gap.

ISSUE-003 directly identifies the false equality between the expected Frobenius norm and the product of norms, explains the invalid passage from an asymptotic second-moment ratio to a first-moment equality, and supplies the corresponding asymptotic repair. This is the same failed expectation/square-root inference diagnosed by gold I007.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify that the proof supports only an asymptotic second-moment relation, not the advertised finite-n first-moment equality E||AB||_F=(3/4)||A||_F||B||_F; expectation and square-root operations cannot be interchanged in the asserted way.

component_coverage.gold_component: The displayed second-moment calculation does not establish the advertised first-moment equality; the equality is false because the proof conflates square roots/expectations and random norm products.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly contrasts the deterministic expected norm with the random norm product, identifies the unsupported conversion from second moments to first moments, states that the exact equality is false, and proposes an asymptotic replacement.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 challenges the first-moment equality within the positive-uniform-entry calculation. Gold I008 concerns the proposition's failure to state or establish distributional hypotheses, nonzero-product conditions, and lower-tail or inverse-moment control needed for broad expected-relative-error guarantees. The prediction does not recognize those applicability and reciprocal-norm obligations.
